facts: *The Gambler* is a novel by Fyodor Dostoyevsky.
The eBook edition was released on May 1, 2000.
The edition was produced by Martin Adamson.
The text is organized into seventeen chapters.
The narrator's patrons are a Russian General and his family.
Polina Alexandrovna tells the narrator that her grandmother is dying.
Polina gives the narrator 700 florins to gamble at roulette.
The family hosts entertainments with guests including a French Marquis and Mr. Astley.
The narrator enters a casino for the first time to gamble with money entrusted to him by Polina.
He starts with 100 gülden of Polina's money and accumulates 1,600 gülden.
The General warns the narrator against gambling due to social concerns.
Polina demands they become equal partners in any future gambling.
The narrator has known Polina for three weeks.
The General is waiting for news from St. Petersburg about his mother.
Mlle. Blanche is a Frenchwoman connected to the Marquis.
Mr. Astley shows obvious affection for Polina.
The narrator plays roulette for Polina Alexandrovna using her 600 gülden.
He initially wins 4000 gülden before losing it all.
The narrator lies to the General and the Frenchman about the source of the money.
He criticizes German industriousness while defending Russian gambling habits.
The Marquis de Griers has ceased his attentions because the General is mortgaged to him.
Mademoiselle Blanche will never marry the General.
Polina is in debt and needs to win at the gaming tables.
The narrator obeys Polina's command to insult the Baroness Burmergelm.
The narrator has been infatuated with Polina for four months.
The narrator declared himself the slave of Baron and Baroness Burmergelm in French.
The General fired the narrator and provided severance of forty gülden.
The narrator's true motivation for his actions was to impress Polina.
The narrator instructs his hotel maître d'hôtel to send bills directly to him.
De Griers arrives as an emissary from the General to dissuade the narrator from confronting the Baron.
The narrator plans to engage Mr. Astley as his second for a formal dispute.
Polina urges the narrator to abandon his plan through a note delivered by De Griers.
The narrator confesses his love for Polina for the first time at a café.
Mlle. Blanche de Cominges is the General's fiancée.
Blanche was expelled by casino authorities after losing money.
Astley theorizes that Blanche seeks to marry the General to escape her disreputable past.
Antonida Vassilievna Tarassevitcha is a seventy-five-year-old wealthy Moscow landowner.
She arrives at a luxury spa hotel carried in an armchair due to her inability to walk.
Antonida questions the General about his finances, suspecting he is squandering the family's money.
She declares her intention to explore the spa town and demands an escort.
The Grandmother registered under a false title at a European spa.
She won 4,200 gülden after betting on zero at the casino.
The Grandmother commanded Alexis to stake 4,000 florins on red.
Her total winnings reached 12,000 florins after winning twice consecutively.
The Grandmother wins 12,000-13,000 florins at the roulette table.
She tells the General he will receive nothing from her.
Polina hands the narrator a letter for Mr. Astley.
Mlle. Blanche tries to charm the narrator into discouraging the Grandmother from gambling.
The Grandmother lost 12,000 gülden at roulette.
She converted securities into an additional 12,000 florins.
The Grandmother lost approximately ten thousand roubles gambling alone that night.
She gave Alexis Ivanovitch five hundred gülden before summoning him back.
The Grandmother loses nearly 90,000 roubles at the Casino.
She borrows 3,000 francs from Astley.
The Grandmother departs by train on the 9:30 train.
Blanche has already packed to leave for Paris the next morning.
Polina brings a letter from De Griers to the man's hotel room.
The narrator realizes that Polina loves him, not Mr. Astley.
He wins approximately one hundred thousand florins at the Casino.
The narrator presents his winnings to Polina, who is waiting on the sofa.
The narrator wins 200,000 francs at the gambling table.
Polina throws 50,000 francs in the narrator's face.
Mlle. Blanche demands 50,000 francs from the narrator.
The narrator departs for Paris with Mlle. Blanche and her mother.
The narrator spends 200,000 francs on Mlle. Blanche during his stay in Paris.
Blanche takes 100,000 francs in cash from the narrator.
Blanche manipulates the General into marriage by posing as a potential heiress.
The narrator plans to travel to Homburg to gamble after Blanche's wedding.
The narrator is a Russian gambler in Homburg.
Polina, the woman the narrator loved, is now in Switzerland with her family.
Mr. Astley criticizes the narrator's gambling and refuses to enable him.
The narrator once staked his last gülden and won 170 gülden.
